metadata.query: What happened between Verstappen and Hamilton at Turn 4 during the 2021 Brazilian GP?

data.query: What happened between Verstappen and Hamilton at Turn 4 during the 2021 Brazilian GP?
data.summary:
During the **2021 São Paulo Grand Prix** (Brazilian GP) on **November 14, 2021**, a highly controversial battle for the lead occurred between title rivals Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen [1.8]:

* **The Incident (Lap 48):** Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) used DRS to launch an overtake on the outside of Max Verstappen (Red Bull) heading into Turn 4 [1.2, 1.3]. In response, Verstappen braked exceptionally late on the inside, ran wide, and forced both himself and Hamilton completely off the track onto the run-off area [1.2, 1.3]. Verstappen rejoined ahead and retained the lead [1.3]. 
* **The Immediate Decision:** The FIA stewards "noted" the incident during the race but opted against a formal investigation, aligning with the "let them race" philosophy [1.3, 1.7, 1.10]. However, FIA Race Director Michael Masi admitted post-race that the stewards made this decision without having access to the forward-facing onboard camera from Verstappen's car [1.7].
* **The Right of Review (Article 14.1.1):** On November 16, 2021, Mercedes petitioned for a "Right of Review" under Article 14.1.1 of the FIA International Sporting Code [1.3]. They presented the newly released, high-definition forward-facing onboard footage of Verstappen’s steering wheel to argue he intentionally drove Hamilton off the road [1.5].
* **The Final Verdict:** On November 19, 2021, the stewards denied Mercedes’ request [1.2]. They ruled that while the footage was "new" and "relevant," it was not "significant" enough to alter their original decision [1.2, 1.6].

**Quotes & Aftermath:**
* **Max Verstappen:** *"I thought it was fair, hard racing... we were fighting hard, braking late into the corner, the tyres were quite worn. If I would have turned more abrupt to the left, you just spin off the track."* [1.6]
* **Toto Wolff (Mercedes Team Principal):** Called the denied appeal *"completely expected,"* but added, *"we wanted to trigger a discussion around it, because probably it will be a theme in the next few races."* [1.2]
* **Race Resolution:** Despite the Lap 48 defense, Hamilton successfully overtook Verstappen on Lap 59 and went on to win the Grand Prix [1.2, 1.3].
